name: scriggo-2f437fb8-blind25-ots
instr:
# scriggo-regen

An application uses this to embed a scripting layer and to render pages, and both halves now come back wrong in a number of places. Nothing about the embedded language has moved and nothing about the surrounding application has been touched. Sources that used to build and run correctly now produce the wrong output, and in several places something that used to be accepted is refused outright.

Handing a host's own values and code in before anything runs. Preparing the ready-made storage for a build's top-level declared names is off by one: an empty list of declared names gives back a non-empty result instead of nothing, and exactly one declared name gives back a collection whose first entry is a freshly made zero rather than the name that was declared, so a pointer supplied as the backing store is no longer what the running code reads and writes. The other entry point, the one that also takes a lookup table of starting values keyed by name, fails differently: a starting value whose kind lines up with what was declared is now rejected, while a truth value where a whole number was declared, or a nil pointer, is swallowed silently instead of raising the named complaint about that starting value. The separate tool that writes out the source exposing a standard-library unit to the engine misbehaves twice: asked to expose such a unit under an alternative import path it reports a failure even though nothing actually fails and no complaint is printed, and for a unit h
